verdict.reasoning: Patient reports “really bad tummy ache… at the lower bottom of my belly… lower abdomen… below [the belly button]… It’s there all the time… It may be a eight… Few days ago… getting worse big time,” matching constant lower abdominal pain below the umbilicus for a few days, worsening, rated 8/10.

Patient says, “I feel like vomiting, but I… get nauseated, but I don't vomit,” and “My period stopped… last two weeks ago, but… this is different… light pink colour,” indicating nausea without vomiting and light pink vaginal bleeding after the last menstrual period.
When asked about discharge, patient states, “Just very small, extra, like, a vaginal discharge,” which supports slight vaginal discharge.
Regarding bowels: “last week I had problems… I was constipated for a week… What about this week? … that seems to be OK. It's fine now,” confirming constipation last week that has resolved.

To “any problems passing water?” patient says “No,” but then adds, “I have noticed that I don't really go up that high before, so, yeah, I do drink a lot though,” suggesting some change in urinary frequency. Stating “No urinary problems reported” ignores this reported change.

Doctor asks about difficulty breathing or shoulder pain; implied patient response is negative (“No.” captured on doctor line, but consistent with flow). Doctor asks if she feels feverish or faint on standing and patient replies “No” to both. This supports no fever, shortness of breath, shoulder-tip pain, or presyncope.

Patient states, “Yeah, yeah, my regular activities OK… I work regular other activities, like cooking and stuff, everything… but it seems OK,” indicating no issues eating/drinking and intact activities of daily living.
On LMP: “last month, two weeks ago… about two weeks, two or three weeks ago” and confirms “Yeah” when asked if last period was normal, matching a normal period approximately 2–3 weeks ago.

Contraception: “it's called implant… Yes, I do [have periods]… they are spreading like, not the time. It changes,” indicating irregular cycles while on an implant for about a year; doctor later confirms “Implanon was just put in a year ago?” patient: “Yes.”
When asked, “Anything else? Have you had any operations?” patient replies “No,” supporting no past surgical history.
Patient says, “Yeah, I have allergy, I have amoxicillin. Amoxicillin allergy,” which directly supports amoxicillin allergy.
In response to “what's your job day to day?” patient says, “Yeah, I'm a teacher. School teacher,” supporting that she is a school teacher.
To “who do you live with at home?” patient replies, “My husband, and my husband's family,” directly matching the fact.
When asked, “You take any other drugs?” patient replies, “No,” which supports no recreational drug use.
On travel: doctor asks, “Have you been abroad recently?” patient: “Yes… A year ago, not recently. No,” supporting travel abroad about one year ago.

Synthesis of HPI: constant, worsening lower abdominal pain (“lower abdomen… It's there all the time… It is getting worse”), per vaginal spotting/light bleeding (“light pink colour”), nausea without vomiting (“get nauseated, but I don't vomit”), and “very small… vaginal discharge,” all match the assessment description.
Doctor states, “we can arrange a face to face examination where they can… do a abdominal examination,” confirming a face-to-face clinic appointment for abdominal exam.

Doctor asks, “would you be happy to call the support line and arrange that appointment?” and later, “if you call the support line and make an appointment,” confirming patient is to call support line to schedule.
Doctor says, “The other thing we would need to do is to, to do a pregnancy test today, if possible.” Patient: “I will do it,” supporting a urine pregnancy test today.
Doctor advises, “if you can do that today, and if it's positive we need to see you straight away, so give us a call back,” matching immediate call back for urgent review if positive.
Doctor states, “if it gets a lot worse, or you're not holding any fluids down, then we should see you before then,” providing safety-net advice about worsening pain and inability to keep fluids down.
